title: Moving to New Orleans in 1923 and musician neighbours on St. Philip
summary: He moved to St. Philip Street around 1923 and recalls where Kid Howard, Jim Robinson and Jim Hill lived.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When did you move over to New Orleans then?
Well, I moved over in Yarlene. When I moved to New Orleans, I moved to New Orleans in about 1923. Right before you started on the river.
Yeah. When I moved to New Orleans.
And I got over there and I made friends with Howard and all of them when I liked the city and I stayed over there.
Was that St. Philip or DuMaine Street you were living on the time that year?
That was St. Philip between Ramport and St. Claude.
I knew it was up in there somewhere.
Yeah. And Howard. What was the house number?
Remember that now?
What, what that house number was? 1131. 1131. 1131.
I probably had with my old north.
Yeah.
1121. 1121. I remember. Been a good while, you know. 1121. Now, Howard was living right across the street from here. Yeah, that's right.
Yeah.
Jim Robinson too, wasn't he? Jim Robinson was staying across that.
Or close there anyway.
No, he wasn't staying across the street then. He was on Marais first. He was on Marais first.
He was on Marais street then. One time he lived in a double house, though, after that. He did.

Yeah. And then after I left, due to war, he was staying with Kid Howard. Yeah, that's what I mean, he moved. Yeah, that's when he stayed across the street from, but I had left then. Yeah, you left then. Uh, so I played with a lot of fellas.
Jim Hill was up in that section there too. Yeah.

The bass player. The bass player was, he was down between Libby and Marais. Yeah, he was there. Yeah, I think he's still there yet if you all can move. No, he moved this summer. Did he? I don't know where. I don't have his address. Oh, yeah. Jim Robinson knows, I'm sure.
I haven't found out where he lives.
Yeah. Just moved this summer.
